title: Minor repairs and materials suitability
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: Queensland Government (Fair Trading), Apply for a security equipment installer licence (last updated 21 October 2026); NSW Police Force (SLED), Locksmith licensing FAQ (Class 2C) (no date shown).
audience: Property manager partner workers who carry out or approve minor repairs
learningOutcomes: Decide whether a minor repair fits the worker's skill, tools, manufacturer instructions and the property's permissions.
Recognise fire-rated and security items that must be referred rather than adjusted.
Select materials that suit the substrate, the load and the environment.

instruction.heading: Four checks before a minor repair
instruction.body: Before any minor repair, check four things. First, the permission: is the owner or manager approving this exact repair in writing? Second, the skill: does the worker have the training and experience for this task? Third, the manufacturer instructions: does the product or item have instructions, and do they allow this repair? Fourth, the item itself: is it a fire-rated, security or regulated item? If any check fails, the repair is referred. A minor repair is only minor if all four checks pass.

instruction.heading: Materials that suit the job
instruction.body: Choose materials for the substrate, the load and the environment. A fixing for a damp area should resist corrosion. A filler for a wet area should be suited to damp. Small fasteners can have safety-critical functions, such as holding a closer, a hinge or a grab rail. Replace a missing or damaged fastener with one of the same type and rating, and do not substitute a smaller or cheaper item. Keep the product record so that the next person knows what was used.

instruction.heading: When the item is rated or regulated
instruction.body: A security lock or access system controls who can enter. Both are referred to a competent person, and the state licence position for security and locking work is recorded in “Doors, hinges and hardware upkeep”. Do not adjust a rated item because it looks like a simple fix, and do not replace it with a non-rated part.

procedure: Confirm the four checks: permission, skill, manufacturer instructions and item type.
If any check fails, record the refusal or referral and tell the approver.
Choose a material matched to the substrate, the load and the environment, and record it.
Replace a fastener with one of the same type and rating.
Refer any fire-rated or security item rather than adjusting it.
Record the repair, the material and the result.

workedExamples.situation: The owner asks for a quick adjustment to a door closer that is loose on a fire-rated door, and says it is only a small job.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Does the repair pass the four checks?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The permission is only verbal, the item is a fire-rated door closer, and the worker cannot confirm the manufacturer instructions allow the adjustment in this case. Refer the adjustment to a competent person, record the request and the referral, and quote it separately.

equipmentAndPpe: Fasteners and materials matched to the substrate
Manufacturer instructions or data sheets for the item

commonErrors.error: Treating a loose fastener on a rated item as minor.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the item type first, and refer if it is fire-rated or security-related.

commonErrors.error: Substituting a smaller or cheaper fastener.
commonErrors.prevention: Replace with the same type and rating.

commonErrors.error: Doing a repair on a verbal approval.
commonErrors.prevention: Obtain written approval before any repair.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Fire-rated doors and their hardware are part of a fire safety system and are referred to a competent person. This lesson grants no authority to alter them.

Security locks and locking systems: in Queensland, removing and reinstalling household locks needs a security equipment installer licence, except where the building is being constructed, repaired or renovated (Queensland Government page, last updated 21 October 2026). In New South Wales, the NSW Police SLED page (no date shown) treats the Class 2C licence as the requirement for individual locksmiths.
Completing this lesson does not give a locksmith, security, fire safety or building licence, certificate or authority.

qualityStandard: The four checks are recorded before any minor repair.
Every fastener and material used is recorded with its type and rating.
Every fire-rated or security item is referred and not adjusted as minor work.
documentationEvidence: Referral note for any rated or security item
summary: A repair is minor only when permission, skill, manufacturer instructions and the item type all pass.
Match materials and fasteners to the substrate, the load and the environment.

knowledgeChecks.question: The owner asks for a quick adjustment to a loose closer on a fire-rated door. What is correct?
options: Adjust it because the owner asked, and the owner pays for the job
Refer the adjustment to a competent person and record the referral
Replace it with a cheaper closer that the owner can buy from the shop
Adjust it quickly before the owner changes their mind

knowledgeChecks.question: A fastener on a grab rail is missing. What should be used?
options: A smaller screw that fits the hole neatly
Any screw in the drawer that fits
Adhesive only, with no screw at all
A fastener of the same type and rating
